interview.title: G. Lkhagvasuren: Sound legal advice is the compass that guides the future of your business
interview.intro: An interview with G. Lkhagvasuren, Founding Partner and Attorney at Tsets Partners, a professional law firm providing legal advisory services for the day-to-day operations of businesses.
interview.imageAlt: G. Lkhagvasuren, Founding Partner and Attorney at Tsets Partners

sections.title: Tsets Partners and Its Practice
paragraphs: Established in 2017, Tsets Partners Law Firm currently operates two offices in Ulaanbaatar and employs four attorneys and six legal assistants. Over the past eight years, the number of organizations maintaining long-term cooperation with the firm has continued to grow.

Regular clients include Alco Group, Practical Insurance, Milaya Foods, and the Agricultural Corporation SOE LLC. The firm provides ongoing legal advice, debt recovery support, contract drafting and negotiation, assistance in tender procedures, dispute resolution, and other legal support across business activities.
sections.quote: In the day-to-day operations of businesses, numerous legal risks arise, particularly when entering into major contractual arrangements. Our priority is to anticipate such uncertainties and ensure that contracts clearly stipulate solutions to potential disputes.

sections.title: Education and Professional Experience
paragraphs: G. Lkhagvasuren obtained a Master’s degree in Business Administration from the University of Finance and Economics between 2020 and 2022. He continues to manage Tsets Partners LLC while pursuing doctoral studies in law at the National University of Mongolia.
He specializes in insurance law and previously served as Head of the Claims Department at Practical Insurance for four years, gaining extensive professional experience in the insurance sector.

Entrepreneurs who address legal uncertainty at the earliest stage and seek professional advice can protect themselves from many potential risks. Legal services are comparable to chess: they are a strategic tool that enables you to foresee risks three moves ahead.

sections.title: Research on Court Decisions in Insurance Disputes
paragraphs: G. Lkhagvasuren published a research paper titled “Analysis of Court Decisions in Insurance Disputes” on the Legal Data platform. It examines how Mongolian courts resolved insurance-related disputes between 2019 and 2024.

A similar study was conducted in Mongolia in 2016. By 2024, however, both the business environment and insurance contracts had changed significantly, making it necessary to examine how courts currently resolve such disputes.

Since 2019, he has taught Insurance Law and the Application of Law to senior law students at Ikh Zasag International University. He selected three students as assistant researchers for the project. The report gives citizens a general understanding of insurance issues and provides legal practitioners with practical guidance on judicial interpretation and application.

The study found that most insurance disputes arise when policyholders cannot obtain compensation. In more than 70 percent of the disputes studied, courts ruled in favor of compensation. The findings indicate that insurers sometimes refuse claims without sufficient legal grounds, while many people do not pursue litigation because they perceive it as burdensome.

sections.title: International Cooperation
paragraphs: In 2025, the firm planned to enter into cooperation agreements with law firms in the People’s Republic of China. Many Mongolian companies receive investment, equipment, and materials from China, and the two countries maintain extensive cooperation across multiple sectors. Because many of the firm’s clients are Chinese citizens and legal entities, cooperation with Chinese law firms has become a practical necessity.
The firm is also working to increase the number of Chinese-speaking lawyers so that legal teams from both jurisdictions can cooperate effectively when cross-border disputes or other matters arise.

sections.title: Professional Values
paragraphs: G. Lkhagvasuren believes that law firms should not rely heavily on self-promotional marketing and that word-of-mouth is the most effective form of reputation. Clients should feel that every possible effort has been made on their behalf. Genuine, continuous relationships in which clients feel they have a personal attorney are the strongest form of professional trust.

Legal practice can also involve psychological reassurance. People often seek help while facing serious debt or unjust liability. Once they understand their legal protections, rights, and obligations, they can leave with renewed confidence and hope. Providing that support alongside legal advice is one reason he takes pride in the profession.
sections.quote: Attorneys not only protect people from losses caused by a lack of legal knowledge; they also help create economic stability and peace of mind by safeguarding their legal rights and interests.

interview.note: The general firm profile states that Tsets Partners has 12 lawyers, while the interview published on June 10, 2025 refers to 4 attorneys and 6 legal assistants. The interview figures are therefore retained together with their publication date.
